title: Workday Unveils Autopilot Agents, a Headless Agent Platform and New Decision Tools at Rising 2026
source_used: iTWire (Workday Rising analysis, 16 Oct 2026) and InformationWeek (16 Oct 2026); Enterprise Times was blocked
key_facts: At Workday Rising 2026 in Las Vegas (keynote 13 Oct) Workday announced autopilot AI agents built to work on their own, around the clock, in the background.
Joel Hellermark, Workday's chief AI officer: 'Our agents work like autopilots, they get the work done on their own, and bring people in exactly when their judgement makes the difference.'

Workday sorts work into three tiers: humans in the loop for decisions that affect income and employment (it does not automate hiring decisions), on the loop for routine approvals, and out of the loop for tasks such as transaction sampling and compliance checks.

Workday is going 'headless' and surrounding its architecture with an agent platform; Sana, its agentic experience, uses the Model Context Protocol to work inside Microsoft Copilot, Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise and Slack (InformationWeek).
A talent acquisition autopilot agent is now in early access; outreach to candidates requires recruiter approval (iTWire, InformationWeek).
Workday also announced it is acquiring C1.ai, an agentic identity platform for people and agents (InformationWeek).
Chief executive Aneel Bhusri said there is 'always a human in the loop'; Workday's recent quarterly results showed a near 13% revenue increase while it has been cutting head count (InformationWeek).
The benefit claims are Workday's own; the conference drew about 17,000 HR, ERP and IT professionals (InformationWeek).
quote_evidence: "Until now, AI has worked like a copilot, helpful, but only when you ask it something. That's not enough anymore," said Workday Chief AI Officer, Joel Hellermark.
Workday also announced it is acquiring C1.ai, an agentic identity platform for people and agents, following another trend.
The company also introduced a talent acquisition autopilot agent, which is now in early access.
why_it_matters_hint: A major HR and finance software maker is moving from AI assistants to agents that act without being asked, with stated limits on hiring decisions.
notes: Quote evidence for the first item uses the straight apostrophe as printed by iTWire. Both outlets are trade/analyst coverage of Workday's own announcements.
